passages.original: II. Quam testamenti sui ordinationem prædicto Arii satelliti tradidit, Constantio reservandam. Qui dum post sui genitoris obitum adveniens suscepisset imperium, sicut a Constantino fuerat delegatum, Constantio testamentum contradidit. Quin ob bujus rei gratiam, in tanta apud eum idem Evangelus presbyter familiaritate est habitus, ut non jam presbyter, sed pater imperii vocaretur : et qui ob imperandum imperator fuerat elevatus, sub hujus presbyteri im- perio videbatur addictus.
passages.english: II. This disposition of his will he handed over to the aforesaid henchman of Arius, to be kept for Constantius. When Constantius, arriving after his father's death, had taken up the empire, [the presbyter] delivered the will to Constantius, just as it had been entrusted [to him] by Constantine. Indeed, on account of this service, the same presbyter Evangelus was held in such intimacy with him that he was called no longer presbyter but father of the empire; and he who had been raised up as emperor in order to rule seemed to be made subject under the command of this presbyter.
passages.notes: 'bujus' read as 'hujus' (scanning error). The presbyter is named Evangelus here; the name is not otherwise identified.

passages.original: Probus judex dixit : Si ecclesiasticæ consuetudinis mos est ut aliqua verborum vocabula ob coercendos hæreticorum motus in fidei auctoritate nude ponantur, qux tamen ratione ex consequentia rerum existentium vestiantur; dum eorum veritas, ex qua originetn sumunt, divinis contineri litteris invenitur; quid dicis, Ari? Concedis homousion (sicut Athanasius dicit) de divinis Scripturis per convenientes professionum qualitates probari, an non ?
passages.english: Probus the judge said: If it is the custom of the Church's practice that certain words and terms, in order to check the movements of heretics, are set down bare in the authority of the faith, which are nevertheless clothed with reason from the consequence of existing things, provided that their truth, from which they take their origin, is found to be contained in the divine writings, what do you say, Arius? Do you grant that the homoousion, as Athanasius says, is proved from the divine Scriptures through fitting qualities of [their] declarations, or not?
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'qux' read as 'quae', 'originetn' as 'originem'. 'homousion' is the Greek term 'of one substance'. The phrase 'per convenientes professionum qualitates' is obscure; the rendering is tentative.

passages.original: Volente igitur Deo, corruptibilis naturae Virgo, sine ullo pudoris damno filium generavit: et ipse qui incomparabiliter cunctis naturis incorruptibilior permanet, hoc sibi praestare non potuit, ut de sua substantia Filium incorruptibiliter generare potuerit? Ergo quia Deum de seipso Filium generasse, et divinarum Scripturarum testantur eloquia, et in sua Arius superiori prosecutione fassus est, judica, virorum optime Probe, quis magis cum divinis conveniat Scripturis; utrumne egn, qui ob hoc unius substantiae cum Patre Filium esse confiteor, quod videlicet ex ipso, et non aliunde dinoscitur natus : et ob hoc rursus incorruptibiliter genuisse profiteor, quia excellentissima .divinae majestatis substantia, per sui ineffabilem potentiam corruptioni subjacere nullatenus potuisset ;
passages.english: So, by God's will, a Virgin of corruptible nature bore a son without any loss to her chastity; and could he who remains incomparably more incorruptible than all natures not grant himself this, that he could beget a Son from his own substance incorruptibly? Therefore, since both the words of the divine Scriptures testify that God begot the Son from himself, and Arius admitted it in his earlier argument, judge, Probus, best of men, which of us agrees more with the divine Scriptures: whether I, who confess that the Son is of one substance with the Father for this reason, namely that he is known to have been born from him and not from elsewhere; and who profess, again, that he begot incorruptibly for this reason, that the most excellent substance of the divine majesty, through its ineffable power, could in no way have been subject to corruption;
passages.notes: 'egn' read as 'ego' (scanning error). The sentence continues in the following passage ('or this man...').

passages.original: Probus judex dixit : Si huic tam validæ et tam certæ prosecutioni Arius nisus fuerit obviare, certum est eum non rationem se qui, sed per verborum irrationabilium camposeffrenatius evagari, qui usque nunc trium substantiarum rationem, ut superius fassus cst (sicut Athanasius permultum unius substantiae documentum ostendi ), per nescio quam nebulosam caliginem circumiens, assertionem suam nequiverit demonstrare.
passages.english: Probus the judge said: If Arius should try to oppose so strong and so certain an argument, it is certain that he is not following reason, but wandering more unrestrainedly through the fields of irrational words. Up to now, going round through some cloudy darkness or other, he has been unable to demonstrate his assertion, the account of three substances, as he confessed above (just as Athanasius showed at great length the proof of one substance).
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'se qui' read as 'sequi', 'camposeffrenatius' as 'campos effrenatius', 'cst' as 'est'. 'ostendi' is probably a misreading of 'ostendit' ('showed'); translated so.
